entry.title: Treasury and IRS announce Opportunity Zone designations for more than 6,500 communities nationwide
entry.summary: Treasury, IRS announce Opportunity Zones designations for over 6,500 communities across America IRS · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe Treasury Department and IRS announced Qualified Opportunity Zone designations for all 50 states, U.S. territories, and the District of Columbia. A total of 6,576 eligible census tracts were nominated and designated, effective January 1, 2027, for ten years. The Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed the Opportunity Zone tax incentive, added enhanced incentives for rural investment, and established a process for redesignation every ten years.

entry.summary: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots Federal Register · Nov 6, 2026 · Rule · Comments close Jan 4, 2027 · Effective Jan 1, 2027The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) issued a final rule updating payment rates and factors for the Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Ambulatory Surgical Center payment system for calendar year 2027. entry.title: IRS adds business payments to Tax Pro Account for authorized professionals
entry.summary: IRS expands Tax Pro Account for business client payments IRS · Nov 6, 2026 · GuidanceThe IRS announced that authorized tax professionals can now make certain payments for business clients through Tax Pro Account. Covered payments include full or partial balances, amended returns, extensions, proposed tax assessments, and federal tax deposits. Previously, professionals could only view business clients' balances and payment activity. Professionals must hold the appropriate authorization for the client and tax matters involved.

entry.title: CFTC Issues Interpretation of Impartial Access Requirements
entry.summary: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation CFTC · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an interpretation of the impartial access requirement for designated contract markets. It states that geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with the Commodity Exchange Act and that requirement. Designated contract markets must stop domestic geographic restrictions that violate the requirement within 30 days or explain to the Division of Market Oversight why compliance is not feasible.

entry.title: CFTC Staff Letter on Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
entry.summary: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements CFTC · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceOn November 5, 2026, the CFTC's Division of Clearing and Risk issued a no-action letter on whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies for daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, such use is permitted if the clearing organization treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements.

entry.title: IRS reminds tax preparers to renew 2027 PTINs before Dec. 31, 2026 expiration
entry.summary: IRS reminder: Tax professionals should renew their PTINs for 2027 IRS · Nov 4, 2026 · GuidanceThe IRS reminds paid tax return preparers to renew their Preparer Tax Identification Numbers (PTINs) for 2027, as current PTINs expire Dec. 31, 2026. Online renewal through the IRS PTIN System takes about 15 minutes and costs $18.75, while Form W-12 can be used for mailed applications. The release also describes other PTIN account features, the voluntary Annual Filing Season Program, and the separate enrolled agent renewal cycle running through Jan. 31, 2027.

entry.title: IRS launches 2026 seminars for tax professionals in online forum
entry.summary: IRS Nationwide Tax Forum Online offers new 2026 seminars IRS · Nov 4, 2026 · GuidanceThe IRS has launched the 2026 Nationwide Tax Forum Online, giving tax professionals access to more than a dozen seminars recorded at this year's forum. Topics include current tax law, IRS procedures, and key issues for the upcoming tax season. Completed seminars earn continuing education credits, and some courses can be audited for free. The lineup includes a seminar on digital asset information reporting.

entry.title: SEC Updates Small Entity Definitions for Investment Companies and Advisers
entry.summary: SEC Adopts Amendments to Update Definitions of Small Entity for Investment Companies and Investment Advisers SEC · Nov 5, 2026 · RuleThe SEC adopted rule amendments changing which registered investment companies, investment advisers, and business development companies count as small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act. The changes raise asset-based thresholds, update how related funds' assets are aggregated, and remove the adviser total assets threshold. entry.title: CFTC and USDA sign agreement to protect the integrity of U.S. farm markets
entry.summary: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets CFTC · Nov 4, 2026 · GuidanceThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture signed a Memorandum of Understanding to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The agreement lets the two agencies harmonize policies, share information more effectively, and expand access to risk management tools. It also supports both agencies in monitoring and identifying structural or potential systemic risks.

entry.title: CFTC Wins Court Order Requiring Texas Man and Firm to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud Case
entry.summary: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud CFTC · Nov 3, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced a default judgment from the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas against Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for a commodities fraud scheme. The court found they solicited and misappropriated over $3 million from participants through false trading claims, Ponzi-like payments, and personal use of funds. The defendants were ordered to pay a $9,767,625 civil penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution, and were permanently enjoined and banned from trading and registration.

entry.title: CFTC Chairman Selig statement on perpetual futures for individual stocks
entry.summary: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures CFTC · Nov 3, 2026 · ReportCFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced that perpetual futures on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets dually registered with the SEC. He said the change lets U.S. participants use these products within the CFTC's regulatory framework instead of offshore venues. The statement cites the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000 and the CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding as its basis.

entry.summary: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing, and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of, a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 17.111(d) (Commodity-Based Trust Shares) Federal Register · Nov 3, 2026 · Licensing · CryptoTopic evidence: 「permit up to 15% of the net asset value of the Trust’s holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria」 The SEC published notice of, and approved on an accelerated basis, a Texas Stock Exchange proposal to amend Rule 17.111(d) and adopt generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares. Under the change, such shares can be listed under Rule 19b-4(e) without a separate filing for each product. The proposal permits up to 15% of a trust's net asset value to consist of certain digital commodities and allows actively managed shares, and the Commission waived the 30-day operative delay. entry.title: Proposed FCC update to ultra-wideband device rules for modern uses
entry.summary: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices Federal Register · Nov 2, 2026 · Draft / consultation · Comments close Dec 2, 2026The Federal Communications Commission proposes updating its rules for ultra-wideband (UWB) devices, which were first adopted in 2002. UWB is now widely used for tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, and public safety. Because the existing rules have not kept pace, the FCC has received a growing number of waiver requests for modern devices. The proposal aims to add flexibility and protect incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users. entry.title: Final rule requiring pharmacy benefit managers to disclose their fees
entry.summary: Improving Transparency Into Pharmacy Benefit Manager Fee Disclosure Federal Register · Nov 2, 2026 · Rule · Effective Jan 4, 2027The Department of Labor issues a final rule requiring pharmacy benefit managers and affiliated brokerage and consulting providers to disclose their compensation to fiduciaries of large, self-insured group health plans under ERISA section 408(b)(2). The disclosures let fiduciaries assess whether service contracts and the providers' compensation are reasonable. The rule takes effect January 4, 2027 and applies to plan years beginning on or after July 1, 2027. entry.title: Bisignano donates $250 to Brooklyn children's Trump Accounts
entry.summary: Frank Bisignano donates to Trump Accounts for children in Brooklyn, NY IRS · Added Oct 30, 2026 · SpeechIRS and Social Security leader Frank Bisignano announced that his family fund will give $250 to every child aged two to eight in Brooklyn zip code 11234. The money goes into each child's Trump Account, invested in a fund tracking top U.S. companies. Trump Accounts are long-term savings investment accounts that grow with the U.S. economy, and parents must activate them before family, friends, or employers can contribute.

entry.title: EPA Proposes Revisions to Oil and Gas Emission Standards and Rescission of Super Emitter Program
entry.summary: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review Federal Register · Oct 29, 2026 · Draft / consultation · Comments close Dec 16, 2026The EPA proposes amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the oil and natural gas sector, responding to reconsideration petitions on its March 2024 rule. The proposal would rescind the Super Emitter Program and revise requirements for well sites, liquids unloading, pumps, fugitive emissions, and storage vessels. Comments are due December 16, 2026, and a virtual public hearing is scheduled for November 13, 2026.
